draft.title: Fascism in Italy
card: After the First World War, Italy faced unemployment, rising prices and strikes. Many Italians felt let down by the peace settlement and feared communism. Liberal governments looked weak.

Benito Mussolini led the Fascist Party. He promised order at home and national glory abroad, a revived Italy that would be strong again. Its armed squads, the Blackshirts, attacked socialists, trade unionists and their offices. This violence made the Fascists feared, and it also won support from people who wanted order.

In October 1922 the Fascists marched towards Rome and demanded power. King Victor Emmanuel III did not order the army to stop them. He asked Mussolini to form a government, so Mussolini took office legally, under threat of force.
Mussolini then built a one-party state. He took the title Il Duce, passed laws that gave him wide powers, and banned other parties. By the late 1920s Italy was a dictatorship.
draft.remember: Fascists promised order and national glory. The king appointed Mussolini legally under threat of force, and he then built a one-party dictatorship.

a.q: By what route did Mussolini come to hold office as Italy's prime minister in 1922?
opts: The king asked him to govern in response to the march
He won a majority of seats in a national election
The army overthrew the government and installed him
Parliament made him dictator before the march began
a.why: The March on Rome put pressure on the government, and while the Blackshirts were still gathering, the king chose to ask Mussolini to form a government rather than use the army. He did not win an election or take power in an army coup. His dictatorial powers came later, after he held office.
a.clue: Think about who had the power to appoint a prime minister.

b.q: Why did the March on Rome succeed in bringing Mussolini to power?
opts: The king did not stop the march and asked him to govern
The army fought the Fascists and lost near Rome
The Blackshirts took Rome by force and removed the king
The Fascists had already banned all other parties
b.why: The march worked because the king did not use the army against it and invited Mussolini to form a government. The Fascists did not defeat the army, because it was never ordered to fight. Banning other parties came after Mussolini took office, as he built the one-party state.
b.clue: Consider what the king did when the Fascists threatened Rome.

a.best: The king asked him to govern in response to the march

b.best: The king did not stop the march and asked him to govern

The clue ('what the king did when the Fascists threatened Rome') gives the answer away: only one option describes the king acting, as opposed to being removed. Question b also tests almost the same fact as question a.

proposal.title: Fascism in Italy
card: After the First World War, Italy faced unemployment, rising prices and strikes. Many Italians felt cheated by the peace settlement, feared communism and saw elected governments as weak.

Benito Mussolini's Fascist Party promised order at home and national glory abroad. Its armed squads, the Blackshirts, attacked socialists and trade unionists, which won support from people who feared revolution.
In October 1922 the Fascists marched on Rome and demanded power. King Victor Emmanuel III did not use the army against them and asked Mussolini to form a government.
As prime minister, Mussolini built a one-party state. He took the title Il Duce (the leader), gained wide powers by law and banned other parties, so by the late 1920s Italy was a dictatorship.
proposal.remember: Fascists won support by promising order and glory, took office through the king under threat of force, then removed all rival parties.

a.q: By what route did Mussolini come to hold office as Italy's prime minister in 1922?
opts: The king asked him to form a government after the march
He won a majority of seats in a national election
The army overthrew the government and put him in charge
The Blackshirts seized Rome and removed the old government
a.why: The March on Rome was a threat, and the king responded by asking Mussolini to form a government rather than using the army. The Blackshirts did not seize Rome by force, and Mussolini did not win an election or come to power in an army coup.
a.clue: Did the march itself take power, or did it pressure someone else to act?

b.q: In 1921 an Italian factory owner fears strikes and a communist revolution. Why might he support the Fascists?
opts: They attacked socialists and promised to restore order
They promised to give factories to the workers who ran them
They pledged to keep many parties competing in elections
They backed strikes as a way to raise workers' wages
b.why: The Blackshirts attacked socialists and trade unionists, and the Fascists promised order, which appealed to people who feared revolution. Handing factories to workers is a communist aim, the opposite of what Fascists offered. The Fascists later banned other parties rather than protecting party competition.
b.clue: Think about what this owner most wants to stop.

a.best: The king asked him to form a government after the march

b.best: They attacked socialists and promised to restore order
